summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) is in a tense pause: there are no confirmed US or Israeli strikes on Iran in recent weeks, but Iran is still attacking ships around the Strait of Hormuz, the US blockade of Iranian ports continues, and talks on a new draft deal are under way. Hormuz is open only in part, with oil flows well below normal.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are open under US control. Most ships now pass through a US-run transit system (101 transits over Oct 22–24, against about 138 a day in 2025), with only a handful a day outside it.

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: Around 11.6 to 11.7 million barrels a day in October, against about 17.1 million before the war (Kpler).

status.label: The war
status.note: No confirmed US or Israeli strikes on Iran in recent weeks (AFP reported none on Iranian targets since early September). Trump said on Oct 8 the US would not resume strikes before the Nov 3 midterms; reports say renewed strikes are being prepared for after that.

status.label: Brent crude
status.value: About US$117 (expiring December contract); about US$113.6 for January
status.note: The December contract, which expires on Oct 30, was near US$117.15 in early US trading (Kitco, about 9:10 a.m. ET), on course for a monthly gain of about 13%; Trading Economics showed Brent at US$113.61, up 2.5% on the day, and Yahoo Finance put Brent near US$113 and WTI near US$104 after the US open.

updates.text: UKMTO's weekly overview counted 122 outbound and 155 inbound transits of the strait in the latest seven days, up from 114 and 127 the week before; traffic remains about 70% below pre-war levels.
Oman's navy evacuated 25 crew from a Panama-flagged commercial vessel that was targeted and caught fire about 1.6 nautical miles off Musandam, at the Strait of Hormuz.
Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday for another round of talks on ending the war; Iran is expected to answer a revised Qatari proposal by the end of the week. No agreement has been reached.
sources: Euronews, Oct 30: Iran's Revolutionary Guard reports tankers on fire in Strait of Hormuz as talks continue
ABC News live updates: Qatari delegation arrives in Iran to continue talks

updates.text: Iran's navy said it hit and destroyed an 'enemy submarine' east of the Strait of Hormuz, and state media said two oil tankers caught fire there after striking mines; Major General Yazidi said the strait 'will remain closed until Iran's conditions are met'. There was no independent confirmation and no US comment.
sources: The Tribune (ANI), Oct 30: Iranian Navy says it destroyed 'enemy submarine' and damaged two oil tankers

updates.text: Trump said in a morning interview that the Iran war would end 'one way or another' soon and that gasoline prices would fall; Al Arabiya, citing sources, reported the US told mediators that Iran giving up its nuclear program is the basis for talks. No agreement has been announced.
sources: investingLive, Oct 30: Morning Kickstart: tech hammered as Amazon and Intel tumble; oil rises despite peace talk

updates.text: In a later statement the Revolutionary Guards said a supertanker carrying two million barrels of oil stopped after an explosion, calling it 'the third oil tanker to have exploded and caught fire today'; ship names were not given.
sources: Arab News (Reuters), Oct 30: Iran Guards say three tankers halted in Hormuz
Euronews, Oct 30: Iran's Revolutionary Guard reports two tankers on fire in Strait of Hormuz as talks continue

updates.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers were halted south of the Strait of Hormuz after unspecified 'incidents' while using a route Tehran calls unauthorised, saying the ships had switched off their tracking systems and ignored radio warnings; there was no US or UKMTO comment.
sources: Arab News, Oct 30: Iran Guards say two tankers halted after 'incidents' in Hormuz
Dhaka Tribune, Oct 30: Iran Guards say two tankers halted after 'incidents' in Hormuz

updates.text: UKMTO reported that a small boat attached two explosive devices to an outbound tanker about 25 nautical miles northeast of Khasab, Oman, on Oct 29; the blasts caused an engine-room fire, the crew was safe and the ship resumed its voyage. EOS Risk Group identified the ship as the LOUISE 1 and the devices as limpet mines.
sources: gCaptain: Tanker hit by limpet mines in Strait of Hormuz

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
